introduction: Othello, a Moorish general serving Venice, has secretly married Desdemona just as a Turkish threat requires him in Cyprus. Their marriage faces her father's hostility, but a more intimate danger comes from Iago, an officer Othello trusts. Passed over for promotion, Iago uses the disappointed suitor Roderigo and watches for ways to turn ordinary kindness into suspicious evidence. Once the company reaches Cyprus, military celebration and private courtship become opportunities for a deception that tests the general's confidence in his wife.

fullSynopsis.text: Iago resents Othello for choosing Cassio as lieutenant. With Roderigo, who wants Desdemona, he rouses her father Brabantio using racist images of her secret marriage. Brabantio accuses Othello of winning her through witchcraft, but Othello tells the Venetian council how she loved the story of his life. Desdemona confirms her choice. The state needs Othello to defend Cyprus and permits her to accompany him. Iago persuades Roderigo to keep financing his pursuit. Privately, he also cites an unverified suspicion that Othello has slept with Emilia, Iago's wife, and plans to suggest intimacy between Desdemona and Cassio.

A storm destroys the Turkish fleet, and the travellers arrive safely in Cyprus. Othello and Desdemona reunite joyfully. Iago treats Cassio's courtesy toward her as material for his plot and falsely tells Roderigo that she loves Cassio. During the celebrations, he pressures the reluctant Cassio to drink and has Roderigo provoke him. Cassio strikes Roderigo and fights Montano, wounding him. Iago gives Othello a selective account that conceals his own orchestration, and Othello dismisses Cassio. Posing as a friend, Iago advises Cassio to seek Desdemona's intercession, intending to make her generous advocacy look like desire.

Desdemona promises to plead for Cassio. When Othello sees Cassio leave her, Iago insinuates guilt, then alternates apparent reluctance with warnings about deception and jealousy. Othello's trust begins to collapse. Desdemona drops the handkerchief Othello first gave her; Emilia picks it up for Iago, unaware of his purpose, and he takes it. He plans to leave it in Cassio's lodging. He invents a story of Cassio speaking of Desdemona in a dream and claims to have seen him use her handkerchief. Othello accepts these suggestions as proof, vows revenge, orders Cassio's death and promotes Iago.

Othello demands the handkerchief while Desdemona continues urging Cassio's restoration, not understanding his suspicion. Cassio, having found it in his room, gives it to Bianca to copy its embroidery. Iago later places Othello where he can watch Cassio laugh about Bianca while believing the conversation concerns Desdemona. Bianca's angry return of the handkerchief seems to confirm the false interpretation. Othello decides to kill his wife, accepting Iago's suggestion that he strangle her in bed; Iago undertakes Cassio's murder. Lodovico arrives with orders recalling Othello and appointing Cassio to govern Cyprus. Othello strikes Desdemona before him.

Emilia insists that Desdemona is faithful, but Othello rejects her testimony and abuses his wife as a prostitute. Desdemona appeals to Iago, who pretends that state business explains the change. Roderigo, frustrated by his lost money and jewels, threatens to expose Iago, but is drawn into another plan: he must kill Cassio to keep Othello and Desdemona from leaving. Iago falsely says their destination is Mauritania. Preparing for bed at Othello's command, Desdemona sings the sorrowful willow song and discusses women's fidelity with Emilia. She dismisses her attendant, remaining devoted to the husband whose conduct frightens her.

Roderigo attacks Cassio but is wounded by him. Iago secretly cuts Cassio's leg, then returns as an apparent rescuer and stabs Roderigo, silencing his accomplice. He tries to direct suspicion toward Bianca. Othello hears Cassio's cries and wrongly believes the promised killing accomplished. He confronts Desdemona in bed and refuses her pleas to question Cassio or spare her. He smothers her. Emilia arrives with news that Cassio lives; Desdemona briefly speaks again, declares herself guiltless and dies while shielding Othello. He then admits the murder, insisting that Iago supplied the grounds for his belief.

Emilia exposes the handkerchief's real route despite Iago's commands to be silent. He stabs her and flees; dying, she reaffirms Desdemona's innocence. Iago is captured, and Othello wounds him but leaves him alive. He asks Cassio's pardon, and Cassio's testimony and Roderigo's papers further reveal the conspiracy. Othello recognizes his disastrous error. Stripped of command and facing confinement, he asks that the state receive a truthful account, then stabs himself and dies upon Desdemona. Cassio governs Cyprus and is charged with deciding Iago's punishment. Gratiano inherits Othello's property, while Lodovico prepares to report the catastrophe to Venice.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Iago tells Roderigo that he hates Othello for promoting Cassio ahead of him. Together they awaken Brabantio with racist accounts of his daughter's marriage, then Iago returns to Othello's side as an apparently loyal servant. Brabantio accuses the general of using magic on Desdemona and brings the charge before the Venetian council, which is urgently considering the Turkish threat to Cyprus. Othello recounts their courtship, and Desdemona publicly affirms her love and allegiance to her husband. The council sends him to Cyprus, with arrangements for her to follow under Iago's care. Iago keeps Roderigo hopeful and paying, then outlines a plot against Cassio and the marriage, also invoking an unproved suspicion of Othello's intimacy with Emilia.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: News of the Turkish fleet's destruction removes the military danger as Cassio, Desdemona and finally Othello arrive in Cyprus. Iago sees an opportunity in Cassio's friendly manners toward Desdemona and persuades Roderigo to provoke him. A herald announces celebrations for the victory and marriage. During the revels, Iago's drinking songs and pressure overcome Cassio's resistance to wine. Cassio becomes drunk, attacks Roderigo and wounds Montano in a fight. Othello arrives to restore order, accepts Iago's apparently reluctant testimony and removes Cassio from office. Iago then recommends that Cassio ask Desdemona to plead for him. Alone, he explains his intention to turn her kindness into apparent evidence of an affair and so entangle all three.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Cassio seeks access to Desdemona through Emilia, and Desdemona promises to restore him to Othello's favour. Iago makes Cassio's departure look furtive and gradually feeds Othello's suspicions through questions, racial insinuations and professions of concern. Emilia finds Desdemona's dropped handkerchief and gives it to Iago without knowing his intended use. He plans to plant it in Cassio's room, then offers Othello invented evidence of Cassio's dream and a claim that he has used the token. Othello vows revenge, demands Cassio's death and names Iago lieutenant. His angry insistence on seeing the handkerchief bewilders Desdemona. Cassio has meanwhile found it in his lodging and asks Bianca to copy the work, arousing her jealousy.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Iago's suggestions drive Othello into a trance. He then arranges for Othello to observe Cassio joking about Bianca while believing he is boasting of Desdemona. Bianca returns the handkerchief, intensifying the false appearance. Othello resolves to murder his wife in bed, and Iago promises to deal with Cassio. Lodovico brings Venice's recall order and witnesses Othello strike Desdemona. Emilia's defense of her mistress cannot dislodge his belief, and Desdemona receives only abusive accusations and Iago's false reassurance. When Roderigo threatens to seek his money back, Iago persuades him to attack Cassio. Before bed, Desdemona sings of abandoned love and talks with Emilia about fidelity, then obeys Othello's command to dismiss her attendant.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: The ambush fails to kill Cassio: he wounds Roderigo, and Iago secretly injures Cassio before returning to murder Roderigo and pose as a helper. Othello wrongly takes Cassio's cries as proof of his death. In the bedchamber he smothers Desdemona despite her denials and pleas. Emilia discovers the murder and exposes Iago's deception, explaining that she gave him the handkerchief. Iago stabs her, but she dies insisting on Desdemona's chastity. Othello wounds the captured Iago and acknowledges Cassio's innocence. Iago refuses further explanation; Cassio's account and Roderigo's letters establish more of the plot. Othello kills himself beside Desdemona. Cassio receives authority over Iago's punishment, and Lodovico undertakes to report the deaths to Venice.
